Taking a Stance on Social Issues

Text Type: Analytical Exposition Text. Materi ini membimbing kamu mengambil sikap secara logis, santun, dan bertanggung jawab tentang isu kesehatan mental remaja, cyberbullying, literasi media, dan keamanan digital.

Essential SkillState a stance, build arguments, evaluate information, and write persuasively.
Language FocusAbstract nouns, causal conjunctions, present tense, modality, and evaluative language.
Final MissionWrite an opinion article or letter to the editor for a digital school magazine.
SubjectBahasa Inggris
Kelas/FaseXI / Fase F
Text TypeAnalytical Exposition
Final ProductOpinion Article / Letter to the Editor
Chapter Opening

When Silence Is Not Enough

Bayangkan situasi ini.

Di grup kelas, seseorang mengirim screenshot percakapan pribadi tanpa izin. Beberapa siswa menertawakannya. Ada yang menambahkan komentar tidak pantas. Ada juga yang hanya membaca tanpa berkomentar, padahal ia tahu bahwa tindakan itu menyakiti temannya.

Di hari lain, sebuah pesan berantai tentang “aturan sekolah baru” tersebar cepat. Banyak siswa langsung percaya dan membagikannya ke grup lain. Setelah dicek, ternyata informasi itu tidak benar.

Sementara itu, seorang siswa terlihat semakin diam. Ia jarang bicara, sering terlihat lelah, dan mulai menjauh dari teman-temannya. Beberapa teman hanya berkata, “Dia malas,” padahal mungkin ia sedang mengalami tekanan yang tidak terlihat.

Should students take a stronger stance on mental health awareness, cyberbullying prevention, and media literacy?

Dalam chapter ini, kamu akan belajar bagaimana mengambil sikap atau taking a stance terhadap isu sosial. Kamu tidak hanya akan berkata “I agree” atau “I disagree”. Kamu akan belajar membangun argumen logis, menggunakan alasan, contoh, dan bahasa yang santun.

Taking a stance means you clearly show your position on an issue and support it with reasons.

Mengambil sikap bukan berarti marah-marah. Mengambil sikap berarti berpikir jernih, peduli, dan berani menyampaikan pendapat yang bertanggung jawab.

Learning Map

Learning Objectives

After learning this chapter, you are expected to be able to:

1

identify the social function of analytical exposition text

2

explain the structure of analytical exposition text: thesis, arguments, and reiteration

3

distinguish issue, stance, reason, evidence, example, and recommendation

4

use abstract nouns in argumentative writing

5

use causal conjunctions to connect ideas logically

6

analyze texts about mental health awareness, cyberbullying, and media literacy

7

discuss social issues respectfully

8

write an opinion article or a letter to the editor

9

present your stance with clear reasons and examples

10

create a responsible digital awareness message for your school community

Connection with CP and ATP

Listening and Speaking

You listen to ideas, respond to social issues, express your stance, and discuss problems respectfully.

Reading and Viewing

You read and analyze opinion texts, articles, posters, infographics, and social media messages.

Writing and Presenting

You write an analytical exposition text, opinion article, or letter to the editor and present your argument clearly.

In this chapter, English is not only a school subject. English becomes a tool to think, care, respond, and take part in public discussion.

Part 2

Social Issue Exploration

What Is a Social Issue?

A social issue is a problem that affects many people in a community.

Social issue = masalah sosial yang berdampak pada banyak orang dalam suatu masyarakat atau komunitas.

cyberbullying
mental health awareness
media literacy
online rumors
digital privacy
excessive screen time
peer pressure
school safety
misinformation
emotional pressure
unhealthy comparison
responsible sharing

Social Issues in Island School Context

1. Information Spreads Fast

In a small island community, news, rumors, and screenshots can spread very quickly. A small misunderstanding in one group chat can become a big issue in the school or village.

2. Internet Access Is Useful but Uneven

Some students may have strong internet access at home, while others depend on certain spots or school connection. This affects how students receive and check information.

3. Privacy Is More Sensitive

In a small community, personal information can easily become public gossip. That is why digital privacy matters.

4. Students Need Safe Support

Some students may feel shy to talk about stress because they are afraid of being judged. A supportive school culture can help students feel safer.

5. Media Literacy Is Important

When students receive viral messages, edited videos, or screenshots, they need to check source, context, usefulness, and possible harm before sharing.

Part 3

Genre Focus: Analytical Exposition Text

What Is Analytical Exposition Text?

An analytical exposition text is a text that presents the writer’s stance on an issue and supports it with logical arguments.

Analytical exposition text = teks yang menyampaikan posisi/pendapat penulis terhadap suatu isu dan mendukungnya dengan argumen logis.

The purpose is to persuade readers that an issue is important, serious, beneficial, harmful, or necessary to consider.

Social Function

to persuade readers that the writer’s idea or stance about an issue is logical and worth considering.

Why Is This Text Important?

express your stance clearly
build logical arguments
discuss social issues responsibly
avoid emotional arguments without reasons
write opinion articles and letters
join public discourse respectfully

Generic Structure

StructureFunctionSimple Explanation
ThesisIntroduces the issue and the writer’s stancePembuka yang menyatakan isu dan posisi penulis
ArgumentsGives reasons, evidence, and examplesBagian yang menjelaskan alasan-alasan pendukung
ReiterationRestates the stance and strengthens conclusionPenutup yang menegaskan kembali pendapat penulis

Analytical Exposition vs Hortatory Exposition

AspectAnalytical ExpositionHortatory Exposition
Main PurposeTo persuade readers that an idea is important or logicalTo persuade readers to do or not do something
EndingReiteration of stanceRecommendation
Example TopicCyberbullying is a serious problem for teenagers.Students should report cyberbullying immediately.
FocusWhy the issue mattersWhat readers should do

Mini Example

PartExample / Arti Contoh
TopicCyberbullying should be taken seriously.
Artinya: Perundungan siber harus ditanggapi dengan serius.
ThesisCyberbullying should be taken seriously because it affects students’ emotional safety.
Artinya: Perundungan siber harus ditanggapi dengan serius karena memengaruhi keamanan emosional siswa.
Argument 1It can cause fear, anxiety, and loss of confidence.
Artinya: Hal itu dapat menyebabkan rasa takut, kecemasan, dan hilangnya kepercayaan diri.
Argument 2It spreads quickly and is difficult to stop because digital posts can be copied and shared.
Artinya: Hal itu menyebar cepat dan sulit dihentikan karena unggahan digital dapat disalin dan dibagikan.
ReiterationTherefore, cyberbullying is not a small joke. It is a serious issue that schools and students must address responsibly.
Artinya: Oleh karena itu, perundungan siber bukan lelucon kecil. Ini adalah isu serius yang harus ditangani sekolah dan siswa secara bertanggung jawab.
Part 4

Analytical Exposition Structure Lab

Activity: Find the Structure

Cyberbullying should be taken seriously in every school. It is harmful because hurtful comments, screenshots, and online rumors can make students feel unsafe. Furthermore, cyberbullying can spread quickly because many students can copy, forward, or save digital content. Therefore, schools need to educate students about digital responsibility and empathy.

PartSentence
Thesis
Argument 1
Argument 2
Reiteration
Answer Discussion
PartSentenceExplanation
ThesisCyberbullying should be taken seriously in every school.It states the writer’s stance.
Argument 1It is harmful because hurtful comments, screenshots, and online rumors can make students feel unsafe.It gives the first reason.
Argument 2Furthermore, cyberbullying can spread quickly because many students can copy, forward, or save digital content.It adds another reason.
ReiterationTherefore, schools need to educate students about digital responsibility and empathy.It restates the importance and suggests direction.

Language Focus 2: Causal Conjunctions

Causal conjunctions are words or phrases that connect causes, reasons, and results. They make your argument more logical.

TypeConnectorsExample / Arti Contoh
Reasonbecause, since, asStudents need media literacy because misinformation spreads quickly.
Artinya: Siswa membutuhkan literasi media karena informasi salah menyebar dengan cepat.
Cause with noun phrasedue to, because ofDue to online pressure, some students feel anxious.
Artinya: Akibat tekanan daring, beberapa siswa merasa cemas.
Resulttherefore, consequently, as a resultThe rumor spread quickly; as a result, many students became confused.
Artinya: Rumor itu menyebar dengan cepat; akibatnya, banyak siswa menjadi bingung.
Additionfurthermore, moreover, in additionFurthermore, schools need to teach digital responsibility.
Artinya: Lebih lanjut, sekolah perlu mengajarkan tanggung jawab digital.
Contrasthowever, althoughSocial media is useful; however, it can spread misinformation.
Artinya: Media sosial itu berguna; namun, media sosial dapat menyebarkan informasi salah.

Incorrect

Students need support because of they feel stressed.

Due to students feel pressure, they need support.

Correct

Students need support because they feel stressed.

Students need support because of stress.

Due to pressure, students need support.

Practice 2: Choose the Correct Connector

  1. Students should check information _____ misinformation can spread quickly. A. because B. because of
  2. _____ online pressure, some students feel anxious. A. Due to B. Because
  3. Cyberbullying can damage confidence. _____, schools should prevent it. A. Therefore B. Although
  4. _____ social media is useful, it can also spread false information. A. Although B. Because of
  5. Students need empathy. _____, they need digital responsibility. A. Furthermore B. Due to
Answers

1. A · 2. A · 3. A · 4. A · 5. A

Language Focus 3: Present Tense and Modality

Analytical exposition often uses simple present tense because it discusses general issues.

  • Cyberbullying affects students’ emotional safety.
  • Media literacy helps students evaluate information.
  • Mental health awareness supports students’ well-being.
  • Online rumors spread quickly in digital spaces.
  • Empathy creates a safer school environment.

Parts 9–11

Model Texts: Analytical Exposition

Model Text 1: Mental Health Awareness Should Be Taught at School

Thesis

Mental health awareness should be taught at school because many teenagers face emotional pressure that is not always visible. Students may look fine on the outside, but some of them may feel stressed, anxious, lonely, or overwhelmed by school tasks, family expectations, friendship problems, or social media pressure. Therefore, schools need to help students understand mental health in a safe and responsible way.

Argument 1

The first reason is that mental health awareness helps students recognize their feelings. Many teenagers do not always know how to explain what they feel. They may only say, “I am tired,” “I do not want to talk,” or “I am not okay.” If students learn about emotional awareness, they can understand that feelings such as stress, anxiety, sadness, and fear should not be ignored. This awareness can help them ask for support earlier.

Argument 2

Another important reason is that mental health awareness can reduce stigma. Some students may think that asking for help is embarrassing or a sign of weakness. This idea is harmful because it can make students hide their problems. In fact, asking for help from a trusted adult, such as a parent, teacher, homeroom teacher, school counselor, or health worker, is a responsible action. Schools should teach students that everyone can experience emotional pressure and everyone deserves support.

Argument 3

Furthermore, mental health awareness can create a more supportive school environment. When students understand empathy, they become more careful with their words and actions. They may stop mocking friends who are quiet, avoid spreading rumors, and offer help when someone looks distressed. In island schools, where students often know each other closely, kindness and privacy are very important. A small comment can travel quickly, but a small act of support can also make a big difference.

Reiteration

In conclusion, mental health awareness should be taught at school because it helps students understand their feelings, reduces stigma, and builds a supportive environment. Schools do not need to turn students into mental health experts. However, schools should help students recognize pressure, respect others, and seek help from trusted adults when needed. Mental health awareness is not about labeling people. It is about creating safety, empathy, and responsibility.

Model Text 2: Cyberbullying Is a Serious Problem for Teenagers

Thesis

Cyberbullying is a serious problem for teenagers because it can hurt emotional safety, damage privacy, and spread quickly through digital platforms. Some students may think that online jokes, negative comments, or shared screenshots are harmless. However, when those actions embarrass, frighten, or shame someone repeatedly, they become a form of bullying.

Argument 1

The first reason is that cyberbullying can damage a student’s confidence. Hurtful comments about appearance, ability, family background, or personal mistakes can stay in someone’s mind for a long time. Unlike face-to-face comments, digital comments can be saved, copied, and shared. As a result, the target may feel unsafe even after leaving school.

Argument 2

Another reason is that cyberbullying violates digital privacy. Sharing a private screenshot, photo, or voice note without permission can harm someone’s dignity. In a small school or island community, this problem can become more serious because information spreads quickly. A private conflict can become public gossip, and the person involved may feel embarrassed or isolated.

Argument 3

Furthermore, cyberbullying weakens empathy in digital communication. When students type behind a screen, they may forget that the person reading the message has real feelings. Therefore, students need to learn digital responsibility. Before posting, commenting, forwarding, or reacting, they should ask: “Could this hurt someone?” and “Do I have permission to share this?”

Reiteration

In conclusion, cyberbullying should not be treated as a small joke. It can hurt confidence, violate privacy, and damage school relationships. Students, teachers, and parents need to work together to prevent cyberbullying. A safe digital space begins with empathy, respect, and responsibility.

Model Text 3: Media Literacy Is Essential in the Age of Information Flood

Thesis

Media literacy is essential in the age of information flood because students receive information from many sources every day. News, videos, captions, memes, and group chat messages can appear quickly on students’ phones. However, not all information is accurate, complete, or fair. Therefore, students need media literacy to evaluate information before believing or sharing it.

Argument 1

The first reason is that misinformation can spread very fast. A short message in a group chat may be forwarded many times before anyone checks the source. In an island community, where people often know each other, one false message can create confusion, fear, or conflict. This shows that students need to pause before forwarding information.

Argument 2

Another important reason is that digital content can be taken out of context. A short video may show only one part of an event. A screenshot may hide the previous conversation. A headline may sound dramatic, but the full article may tell a different story. Due to this problem, students should not judge an issue only from one post.

Argument 3

Furthermore, media literacy helps students become responsible digital citizens. Students should check the source, compare information, read beyond the headline, and ask whether the content is useful or harmful. If students practice these habits, they can reduce the spread of hoaxes and help create a healthier digital environment.

Reiteration

In conclusion, media literacy is not only about using technology. It is about thinking critically, reading carefully, and sharing responsibly. In the age of information flood, students must learn to check before they believe and think before they share.

Main Reading Text: Students Should Think Before Sharing Information Online

Thesis

Students should think before sharing information online because digital messages can affect people’s safety, privacy, and relationships. In the past, information moved slowly from one person to another. Today, a message can move from one group chat to another in seconds. This speed can be useful, but it can also be dangerous when students share information without checking it first.

Argument 1

The first reason is that false information can create confusion. For example, if a student forwards a message about a school rule without confirming it with the teacher, many students may misunderstand the situation. Some may feel worried, while others may spread the message further. Consequently, one unverified message can disturb the school community.

Argument 2

Another reason is that careless sharing can hurt someone’s privacy. A screenshot, photo, or voice note may look simple, but it can contain personal information. Sharing it without permission can embarrass someone or damage trust. In a small island community, this can be more serious because personal stories can quickly become public talk.

Argument 3

Furthermore, responsible sharing helps students become better digital citizens. Students should check the source, read the whole message, ask a teacher or trusted adult, and think about the impact before forwarding anything. These habits show maturity, empathy, and responsibility.

Reiteration

In conclusion, students should not share information online carelessly. Digital speed must be balanced with critical thinking. Before clicking “forward,” students should ask whether the information is true, useful, respectful, and safe. Thinking before sharing is a simple action, but it can protect people and strengthen the school community.

📜 Buka Listening Script

Every day, students receive many kinds of information from social media, group chats, videos, and online posts. Some information is useful, but some can be misleading. That is why media literacy matters for students.

Media literacy means the ability to access, understand, evaluate, and use information responsibly. Students with media literacy do not believe every message immediately. They check the source, read the full context, and compare the information with other reliable sources.

In school life, media literacy is very important. For example, a screenshot may not show the full conversation. A short video may not show what happened before or after the recording. A dramatic headline may make people emotional, but the article may contain different information. Therefore, students should be careful before reacting or sharing.

In island communities, information can travel quickly from one family to another, from one class group to another, and from one village to another. Consequently, false information can create confusion faster. However, students can become part of the solution. They can ask questions, check facts, and remind friends to share responsibly.

In conclusion, media literacy is not only about technology. It is about responsibility, honesty, and critical thinking. Before sharing information, students should ask: Is it true? Is it useful? Is it respectful? Is it safe?

What Is an Opinion Article?

An opinion article is a text that presents the writer’s opinion about an issue and supports it with arguments.

What Is a Letter to the Editor?

A letter to the editor is a short formal letter written to respond to an issue in a newspaper, magazine, school bulletin, digital wall magazine, or blog.

  3. stance,

Model 1: Opinion Article

Students Should Take Digital Privacy Seriously

Digital privacy should be taken seriously by students because online actions can affect real life. Many students share screenshots, photos, or personal stories without thinking about the impact. Although it may look simple, careless sharing can damage trust and hurt someone’s dignity.

The first reason is that private information belongs to the person involved. A screenshot of a chat may contain feelings, problems, or personal details. If it is shared without permission, the person may feel embarrassed or betrayed. This shows that privacy is not only about passwords; it is also about respect.

Another reason is that digital content can spread quickly. Once a photo or screenshot is shared, it can be copied, saved, and forwarded. As a result, students may lose control over their own information. In a small school community, this can become more serious because many people know each other.

Therefore, students should ask for permission before sharing personal content. Schools should also teach digital manners and privacy awareness. In conclusion, digital privacy is part of responsibility. Respecting privacy means respecting people.

Model 2: Letter to the Editor

To the Editor of the School Digital Wall Magazine,

I am writing to express my concern about the way students share information in class group chats. Recently, many messages, screenshots, and rumors have been forwarded without checking the truth or asking for permission.

I believe that our school needs a digital responsibility campaign. The first reason is that misinformation can create confusion among students. For example, when an unverified message about school activities is shared, many students may misunderstand the situation. Furthermore, sharing screenshots without permission can hurt someone’s privacy and confidence.

Therefore, I suggest that our school create simple digital manners guidelines. Students should check information before forwarding it, respect privacy, and avoid hurtful comments. Teachers and student organizations can also remind students through posters, short videos, and class discussions.

In conclusion, a safer digital environment begins with responsible students. I hope our school digital wall magazine can publish more content about media literacy and digital empathy.

Sincerely,
A concerned student

Part 22

Common Mistakes

1. Thesis Is Too General

Weak: Cyberbullying is bad.
Better: Cyberbullying should be taken seriously because it can damage students’ confidence and privacy.

2. Argument Without Reason

Weak: Media literacy is important.
Better: Media literacy is important because it helps students check information before sharing it.

3. Only “I Think” Without Evidence

Weak: I think mental health awareness is good.
Better: I believe mental health awareness is important because it helps students recognize stress and seek support from trusted adults.

4. Wrong Use of Due To

Due to students feel stress, they need support.
Due to stress, students need support. / Because students feel stress, they need support.

5. Wrong Use of Because Of

Students need guidance because of misinformation spreads quickly.
Students need guidance because misinformation spreads quickly. / Students need guidance because of the spread of misinformation.

6. No Reiteration

That is my argument.
In conclusion, digital privacy should be respected because careless sharing can hurt trust, safety, and confidence.

7. Too Emotional Without Logic

People who share hoaxes are terrible.
Sharing hoaxes is harmful because it can create confusion and damage trust in the school community.

8. Blaming the Victim

Victims of cyberbullying should not be too sensitive.
Students who experience cyberbullying deserve support, safety, and help from trusted adults.

9. Unsafe Mental Health Claim

Students who feel stressed are weak.
Students who feel pressured need support, understanding, and a safe space to talk.

Part 24

Quiz Pilihan Ganda A–E

Pilih jawaban yang paling tepat. Soal dibuat berbasis cerita agar kamu memahami konteks penggunaan bahasa.

LOTS1. Naya reads an article titled “Media Literacy Is Important for Students.” The text presents the writer’s stance and gives several reasons why students should check information before sharing it. What is the social function of the text?
LOTS2. Rafi writes the following sentence at the beginning of his text: “Cyberbullying should be taken seriously because it can damage students’ emotional safety.” Which part of analytical exposition is this sentence?
LOTS3. Salsa wants to complete this sentence: “Digital __________ is important because students must protect their personal information.” Which word best completes the sentence?
LOTS4. Read the sentence: “Students should check information before sharing it __________ misinformation can spread quickly.” Which connector is correct?
LOTS5. Read the sentence: “Students should not share screenshots without permission.” What type of sentence is it?
LOTS6. Which sentence is the best reiteration for a text about cyberbullying?
MOTS7. In her article, Dinda writes: “Mental health awareness helps students recognize stress earlier. As a result, they can ask for support before the problem becomes heavier.” What is the main argument?
MOTS8. Which sentence uses “due to” correctly?
MOTS9. A student shares a private screenshot from a classmate’s chat because he thinks it is funny. The screenshot spreads to several groups, and the classmate feels embarrassed. Which stance is most appropriate?
MOTS10. A viral message says that school will be closed for a week. The message has no source, no date, and no confirmation from teachers. Several students forward it immediately. What should a media-literate student do?
MOTS11. A student writes: “Cyberbullying can damage students’ confidence.” Which sentence best supports this argument?
MOTS12. Weak thesis: “Mental health is good.” Which revision is the strongest?
MOTS13. Read the sentence: “A screenshot may not show the full conversation. __________, students should not judge an issue from one screenshot.” Which connector is most suitable?
MOTS14. A student wants to write to the school digital wall magazine about unsafe behavior in group chats. She wants to suggest a school campaign. Which text type is most suitable?
HOTS15. A student writes: “Media literacy is important because viral messages can be false, screenshots can miss context, and students need to check reliable sources before sharing.” Why is this argument strong?
HOTS16. In a class group, someone posts an embarrassing photo of a student. Some friends laugh and add stickers. You want to respond responsibly. What is the best response?
HOTS17. In an island school, a rumor about a student spreads through group chats. Because the community is small, many people hear about it quickly. The information is not verified. Which analytical statement is strongest?
HOTS18. A student writes: “Students who feel stressed are weak and should just be stronger.” Why is this statement inappropriate?
HOTS19. Your class is designing a campaign about cyberbullying prevention. The campaign must be realistic, respectful, and useful for students. Which recommendation is best?
HOTS20. A student’s article argues that media literacy helps students avoid hoaxes, understand context, and share responsibly. Which closing sentence is the best reiteration?

Enrichment Activities

Remedial Activities
